answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity costs scale with influence. Each agent posts a refundable stake that locks for 30 days, and its voting weight is the square root of that stake, so splitting funds across fake accounts gains nothing. Trust flows along a graph: every vertex is an agent, and each edge is a vouch backed by slashable collateral. A river of new accounts with no vouches stays at near-zero weight. To cross the canyon between fringe and core, an attacker must lock real capital and risk losing it to slashing, which makes each fake identity cost more than its influence earns.
